Key Research Thinking Patterns: Multimodal Neuroimaging Biomarker Integration: Combining structural quantification (MTR, deep learning segmentation) with functional mapping (task-based fMRI, seed-based connectivity) to correlate anatomical integrity with clinical outcomes in spinal cord and cognitive disorders.

High-Throughput Interface Engineering for Photovoltaics: Utilizing non-fullerene acceptors (Y7-BO) and density functional theory (DFT) to optimize electron transport layers, thereby enhancing power conversion efficiency and operational stability in inverted perovskite solar cells.

Cross-Domain Neurophysiological Reconstruction: Leveraging high-temporal-resolution EEG combined with cortical source tomography (MNE) and independent component analysis (ICA) to reconstruct resting-state networks and transient neuronal dynamics, bridging the gap between electrical activity and hemodynamic responses.

Segmental Functional Mapping of Sensorimotor Pathways: Applying median nerve electrical stimulation alongside segmental gray matter extraction (C5-C8) to differentiate specific spinal cord reflex arc activations and assess hemispheric lateralization in degenerative conditions.
Summary Description: Lei Ding is a biomedical engineer specializing in advanced neuroimaging and renewable energy materials. In neuroscience, Ding employs multimodal MRI and EEG techniques to quantify spinal cord pathology in Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy and investigate cognitive deficits in Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2. Key methods include deep learning segmentation, task-based fMRI, and cortical source reconstruction. Concurrently, Ding advances perovskite photovoltaics through interface engineering and DFT modeling to enhance solar cell efficiency and stability. This portfolio demonstrates a robust capacity to integrate quantitative imaging biomarkers, neuropsychological assessment, and high-performance material design to address complex neurological and energy challenges.
